_read_me: Package nominal dimensions for kicad_fpcheck.py.  Millimetres throughout.
'span_long_mm'/'span_short_mm' are the footprint's own pad-to-pad outer
span on its two axes, sorted so long >= short -- this is what a correctly
laid footprint's pads should measure, taken directly off KiCad's own
stock footprint for that package (see 'source_geometry' per entry) so the
check compares a footprint against the tool that generated it, not
against a hand-transcribed guess.  'pitch_mm' is the nearest-neighbour
pad-centre spacing within one row/cluster; null where the package has no
repeating row (a two-terminal part has only one spacing, which is
'span_long_mm' minus the pads, i.e. 'gap_mm' below).
'gap_check' is true only for packages whose body directly bridges its two
pads with no real lead frame: chip R/C and MELF terminations, and the
short-gull-wing diode families (SOD-*).  For those, 'gap_mm' is the
measured distance between the pads' facing inner edges, and the rule is:
the body (see 'body_length_mm', from a manufacturer or JEDEC/IPC
citation, independent of the footprint) must be able to reach both pads,
so gap_mm should be a bit LESS than body_length_mm, never more.  A gap
bigger than the body is the failure this table exists to catch: the
keyboard incident in kb/keyboards/diode-footprint-vs-part.md.
'gap_check' is false for every leaded IC and transistor family (SOT,
SOIC, TSSOP, MSOP, QFN, DFN, TO-252).  Their leads do the bridging, not
the body, so a gap-vs-body-length comparison is not physically
meaningful for them; span_long_mm/span_short_mm/pitch_mm/pad_count carry
the check instead.  See kicad_fpcheck.py's module docstring.
'body_length_mm'/'body_width_mm' for a no-lead package (QFN, DFN) equal
the lead-frame envelope by definition (no-lead: the terminal IS the
package edge), so they are read straight off the footprint name/geometry
and cited as such, not to a separate datasheet.
'name_aliases' are case-insensitive substrings used only as the LAST-
resort heuristic (see kicad_fpcheck.py's declared-package priority
order): a footprint name is matched against every package's alias list,
and the LONGEST matching substring wins, so 'SOD-123F' beats 'SOD-123'
on a name that contains both.  This heuristic is the least reliable of
the three declared-package sources and the report says so whenever it is
the one used.

SOD-123.source_geometry: KiCad kicad-footprints, Diode_SMD.pretty/D_SOD-123.kicad_mod, pad (at)/(size): pads at x=+/-1.65mm, size 0.9x1.2mm, retrieved 2026-09-20
SOD-123.source_body: Nexperia SOD123.pdf (package information, rev. 2017-03-16): body 2.675 x 1.6 x 1.15 mm. Diodes Inc SOD123.pdf agrees to within 0.05 mm.
SOD-123.notes: The z_board/hexpad keyboard diode footprint (kb/keyboards/diode-footprint-vs-part.md). gap_mm 2.40 vs body 2.675 leaves only 0.275 mm of body overhanging each pad's inner edge combined (0.14 mm/side) -- little margin. A supplied part even slightly under nominal body length will not visually bridge the pads, which is the reported incident.

SOD-123F.source_geometry: KiCad kicad-footprints, Diode_SMD.pretty/D_SOD-123F.kicad_mod, pad (at)/(size): pads at x=+/-1.4mm, size 1.1x1.1mm, retrieved 2026-09-20
SOD-123F.source_body: mbedded.ninja SOD-123F component-package page, citing manufacturer package drawings: body 3.5 x 1.6 x 1.1 mm (flat-lead variant)
SOD-123F.notes: Flat-lead variant of SOD-123, same footprint FAMILY name but NOT the same body: SOD-123F's body (3.5mm) is LONGER than plain SOD-123's (2.675mm), the opposite of what the 'F' suffix suggests to an unfamiliar reader. Confusing a stock D_SOD-123 footprint with a SOD-123F part (or vice versa) is a family mismatch this table is built to catch via --declared-only, independent of the span/gap numbers. See kb/parts/package-family-traps.md.

SOD-323.source_body: Nexperia/CentralSemi SOD-323 package drawings: body 1.7 x 1.25 x 0.95 mm. SOD-323F (flat lead) shares the same body per the same sources.
SOD-323.notes: Roughly a diode-size step down from SOD-123 (body 1.7 vs 2.675 mm long); the two are visually similar on a render at typical zoom and are a common substitution mistake. See kb/parts/package-family-traps.md.

SOD-80.source_body: Vishay minimelf.pdf (MiniMELF/SOD-80/DO-213AA package information): cylindrical glass body 3.5 x 1.5 mm
SOD-80.notes: Cylindrical MELF body, not a moulded gull-wing part -- the gap_check still applies (the body must physically span the pad gap) but there is no lead frame to inspect for a family mismatch, so heuristic naming is the only family signal for this one.

SOT-23.source_body: JEDEC TO-236 variant AB (per the footprint's own descr field): body 2.9 x 1.3 x 1.0 mm
SOT-23.notes: 3-pin: pitch_mm here is the SAME-SIDE two-pad spacing (1.90 mm), not the commonly-quoted 'half pitch' 0.95 mm figure -- the checker's pitch is a directly-measured nearest-neighbour spacing, so it must be compared against this number, not the marketing figure. gap_check is off; see the module docstring on why a leaded transistor package is not checked body-vs-gap.

SOT-23-5.source_body: JEDEC MO-178 variant AA (per the footprint's own descr field): body 2.9 x 1.6 x 1.1 mm

SOT-23-6.source_body: JEDEC MO-178 variant AB (per the footprint's own descr field): body 2.9 x 1.6 x 1.1 mm

SOT-223.source_geometry: KiCad kicad-footprints, Package_TO_SOT_SMD.pretty/SOT-223-3_TabPin2.kicad_mod, pad (at)/(size); pad span includes the enlarged tab/drain pad which extends past the body for thermal/solder area, retrieved 2026-09-20
SOT-223.source_body: Bourns/CentralSemi SOT-223 package information: body length 6.70-7.30 mm, width 2.85-3.10 mm, nominal values used here
SOT-223.notes: span_long_mm/span_short_mm include the tab pad, which is conventionally drawn larger than the physical tab for thermal relief, so they are not a tight fit check the way the diode families are -- pad_count and pitch carry more weight for this family.

SOT-89.source_body: mbedded.ninja SOT-89 component-package page: body 4.5 x 2.5 x 1.5 mm
SOT-89.notes: needs-verification: span_long_mm/span_short_mm are null because the stock footprint's tab pad did not extract cleanly; only pad_count and pitch_mm are checked for this family. Fill in the spans from a direct read of the footprint before relying on this entry for a span/gap gate.

SOIC-8-N.notes: This is the footprint the Fable-5 blog incident laid down (SOP-8 narrow, 3.9mm body) for a part specified in SOIC-8-W. See kb/parts/package-family-traps.md.

SOIC-8-W.notes: This is the package the Fable-5 blog incident's W25Q128JVS was actually specified in. span_long_mm (12.45 mm) against SOIC-8-N's span_long_mm (6.90 mm) is a 5.55 mm mismatch -- an obviously-FAIL span difference, which is why --declared-only alone (family string comparison, no dimensions needed) already catches this incident.

QFN-16-0.5.notes: Numbered EP: this stock footprint numbers its exposed pad as a plain digit (pad '17'), not as a text ref like 'EP'. kicad_fpcheck.py excludes the largest-area pad from the lead count by an area-ratio heuristic rather than by name; see the module docstring.

DFN-8-0.5.source_body: No-lead package: body = lead-frame envelope = the footprint's own name dimension (3x3 mm)
DFN-8-0.5.notes: Dual-row (2-sided), not 4-sided like a QFN of the same pin count -- span_short_mm (2.40) is the row-to-row extent, not a second body edge, which is why it differs from span_long_mm despite a square 3x3mm body.

GX16-offboard.source_geometry: none: a panel-mount GX16 solder-cup connector has no PCB pads. A board that carries a GX16 pigtail uses wire-solder pads (KiCad Connector_Wire.pretty/SolderWire-*), which are a different part declared on their own.
GX16-offboard.source_body: Handson Technology GX16.pdf (https://www.handsontec.com/dataspecs/connector/GX16.pdf, read via ~/1_projects/dev/hypercardiod_mic/docs/research.md section 3): male connector 35.5 mm total length, 18.3 mm maximum body diameter, thread M16x1, panel nut S19 (19 mm across flats), locking ring thread M16x0.75, solder cup aperture 0.8 mm, maximum cable diameter 5.0 mm, rating 7 A at 125 V.
GX16-offboard.notes: Off-board part: kicad_fpcheck.py reports SKIP for a footprint with no copper pads, and FAIL (pad count) if a design declares this package and lays down pads, which is intended. Panel hole diameter is not stated by the vendor drawing: hypercardiod_mic banded it at 16.2 to 17.0 mm (needs-verification against the purchased part). Keyed or flatted thread variants exist; the cited drawing shows no flat (needs-verification per vendor). Interface rules: skills/hw-design/references/interfaces.md section 11 and kb/interfaces/gx12-gx16.md.

GX12-offboard.source_geometry: none: a panel-mount GX12 solder-cup connector has no PCB pads (see GX16-offboard).
GX12-offboard.source_body: needs-verification: no GX12 manufacturer drawing was read. The name encodes the M12 panel thread (12 mm class, by analogy with the GX16 drawing's M16x1 thread). Body length, nut size and rating must be taken from the purchased part's own drawing before the case phase uses them.
GX12-offboard.notes: Off-board part, same handling as GX16-offboard. Interface rules: skills/hw-design/references/interfaces.md section 11 and kb/interfaces/gx12-gx16.md.
